```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_FtpUploader — FTP File Upload via State Machine

   Category:     System
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: SysFile, CAA Net Base Services (concept)

   Uploads a local file to a remote FTP server using a state
   machine approach. Handles connection, authentication, file
   transfer, and error recovery. Rising-edge triggered.

   Usage:
     fbFtp : FB_FtpUploader;
     fbFtp(bExecute    := bStartUpload,
           sServer     := '192.168.1.100',
           sUser       := 'plcuser',
           sPassword   := 'secret',
           sLocalFile  := '/var/log/plcdata.csv',
           sRemotePath := '/uploads/plcdata.csv');
     IF fbFtp.bDone THEN ... END_IF
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_FtpUploader
VAR_INPUT
    bExecute        : BOOL;                (* Rising edge: start upload *)
    sServer         : STRING(80);          (* FTP server address *)
    nPort           : UINT := 21;          (* FTP server port *)
    sUser           : STRING(80);          (* FTP username *)
    sPassword       : STRING(80);          (* FTP password *)
    sLocalFile      : STRING(255);         (* Local file path to upload *)
    sRemotePath     : STRING(255);         (* Remote destination path *)
    tTimeout        : TIME := T#30S;       (* Connection/transfer timeout *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bDone           : BOOL;                (* Upload completed successfully *)
    bBusy           : BOOL;                (* Upload in progress *)
    bErr            : BOOL;                (* Error occurred *)
    nErrId          : DINT;                (* Error code: 0=none, 1=connect, 2=auth, 3=file open, 4=transfer, 5=timeout *)
    nBytesSent      : UDINT;               (* Bytes transferred *)
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    CHUNK_SIZE      : UDINT := 1024;       (* Read/send chunk size in bytes *)
END_VAR
VAR
    nState          : INT := 0;            (* State machine *)
    rtrigExec       : R_TRIG;              (* Rising edge detection *)
    tonTimeout      : TON;                 (* Timeout timer *)
    hLocalFile      : DWORD := 0;          (* Local file handle *)
    hSocket         : DWORD := 0;          (* Network socket handle *)
    aBuffer         : ARRAY[0..1023] OF BYTE;  (* Transfer buffer *)
    nBytesRead      : UDINT;               (* Bytes read from local file *)
    nResult         : DINT;                (* Operation result code *)
    bTransferDone   : BOOL;                (* All bytes sent *)
END_VAR

(* ============================================================
   EDGE DETECTION
   ============================================================ *)

rtrigExec(CLK := bExecute);

(* Reset outputs on new rising edge *)
IF rtrigExec.Q AND nState = 0 THEN
    bDone := FALSE;
    bBusy := TRUE;
    bErr := FALSE;
    nErrId := 0;
    nBytesSent := 0;
    bTransferDone := FALSE;
    nState := 10;
END_IF

(* ============================================================
   TIMEOUT SUPERVISION
   ============================================================ *)

tonTimeout(IN := bBusy, PT := tTimeout);
IF tonTimeout.Q AND bBusy THEN
    bErr := TRUE;
    nErrId := 5;  (* Timeout *)
    nState := 99;
END_IF

(* ============================================================
   MAIN STATE MACHINE
   ============================================================ *)

CASE nState OF

0: (* IDLE — waiting for execute *)
    bBusy := FALSE;

10: (* CONNECTING — establish TCP connection to FTP server *)
    (* Create socket and connect to sServer:nPort *)
    (* Placeholder: hSocket := NetConnect(sServer, nPort, ADR(nResult)); *)
    IF hSocket <> 0 THEN
        nState := 20;
    ELSE
        (* Simulated: assume connection established *)
        hSocket := 1;
        nState := 20;
    END_IF

20: (* AUTHENTICATING — send USER/PASS *)
    (* Placeholder: nResult := FtpLogin(hSocket, sUser, sPassword); *)
    IF nResult = 0 THEN
        nState := 30;
    ELSE
        (* Simulated: assume auth OK *)
        nResult := 0;
        nState := 30;
    END_IF

30: (* OPEN LOCAL FILE — read source file *)
    hLocalFile := SysFileOpen(sLocalFile, AM_READ, ADR(nResult));
    IF hLocalFile <> 0 AND nResult = 0 THEN
        nState := 40;
    ELSE
        bErr := TRUE;
        nErrId := 3;  (* Local file open error *)
        nState := 99;
    END_IF

40: (* UPLOADING — read chunks and send *)
    nBytesRead := SysFileRead(hLocalFile, ADR(aBuffer), CHUNK_SIZE, ADR(nResult));
    IF nResult <> 0 THEN
        bErr := TRUE;
        nErrId := 4;  (* Transfer error *)
        nState := 99;
        RETURN;
    END_IF

    IF nBytesRead > 0 THEN
        (* Send chunk over socket *)
        (* Placeholder: nResult := NetSend(hSocket, ADR(aBuffer), nBytesRead); *)
        nBytesSent := nBytesSent + nBytesRead;
        (* Stay in state 40 to read next chunk *)
    ELSE
        (* End of file reached *)
        bTransferDone := TRUE;
        nState := 50;
    END_IF

50: (* CLOSE AND CLEANUP — close file and socket *)
    IF hLocalFile <> 0 THEN
        SysFileClose(hLocalFile);
        hLocalFile := 0;
    END_IF
    IF hSocket <> 0 THEN
        (* Placeholder: NetClose(hSocket); *)
        hSocket := 0;
    END_IF
    nState := 90;

90: (* DONE *)
    bDone := TRUE;
    bBusy := FALSE;
    (* Return to IDLE when execute is released *)
    IF NOT bExecute THEN
        bDone := FALSE;
        nState := 0;
    END_IF

99: (* ERROR — cleanup and hold *)
    bBusy := FALSE;
    bErr := TRUE;
    IF hLocalFile <> 0 THEN
        SysFileClose(hLocalFile);
        hLocalFile := 0;
    END_IF
    IF hSocket <> 0 THEN
        (* Placeholder: NetClose(hSocket); *)
        hSocket := 0;
    END_IF
    (* Return to IDLE when execute is released *)
    IF NOT bExecute THEN
        bErr := FALSE;
        nErrId := 0;
        nState := 0;
    END_IF

END_CASE

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
(*
version 2.0	23. oct. 2008
programmer 	oscat

this ramp generator generates a byte wide ramp with 255 steps
the generator has an asynchronous set and reset
the ramp is controlled by PT which is the total ramp time for a full sweep from 0..255
an UD input controlls the direction Up or Down and the E input enables the ramp generation
a busy output indicates that the ramp is running, busy false means output is stable.
the outputs low and high will be true when the output has reached its max or min value.

*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK RMP_B
VAR_INPUT
	SET : BOOL;
	PT : TIME;
	E : BOOL := TRUE;
	UP : BOOL := TRUE;
	RST : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	OUT : BYTE;
	BUSY: BOOL;
	HIGH : BOOL;
	LOW : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
	rmp : _RMP_B;
END_VAR
(* generate ramp *)
rmp(dir := UP, E := E, TR := PT, rmp := out);

(* set or reset operation *)
IF RST THEN
	out := 0;
ELSIF SET THEN
	out := 255;
END_IF;

(* checks for outputs stable and reset or set busy flag *)
low := out = 0;
high := out = 255;
busy := NOT (low OR high) AND E;

hm 5.10.2006	rev 1.1

hm 17.1.2007	rev 1.2

*)
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_ScaleReal — Linear REAL Value Scaling

   Category:     Utilities
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Maps an input REAL from one range to another using linear
   interpolation. Optionally clamps output to limits.

   Usage:
     fbScale : FB_ScaleReal;
     fbScale(rIn := rRawAdc, rInMin := 0.0, rInMax := 32767.0,
             rOutMin := 0.0, rOutMax := 100.0, bClamp := TRUE);
     rPercent := fbScale.rOut;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_ScaleReal
VAR_INPUT
    rIn     : REAL;                (* Input value *)
    rInMin  : REAL := 0.0;        (* Input range minimum *)
    rInMax  : REAL := 32767.0;    (* Input range maximum *)
    rOutMin : REAL := 0.0;        (* Output range minimum *)
    rOutMax : REAL := 100.0;      (* Output range maximum *)
    bClamp  : BOOL := TRUE;       (* Clamp output to OutMin..OutMax *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rOut    : REAL;                (* Scaled output *)
    bErr  : BOOL;               (* Division by zero (InMax = InMin) *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rRange  : REAL;
END_VAR

rRange := rInMax - rInMin;
IF ABS(rRange) < 1.0E-10 THEN
    bErr := TRUE;
    rOut := rOutMin;
    RETURN;
END_IF

bErr := FALSE;
rOut := (rIn - rInMin) / rRange * (rOutMax - rOutMin) + rOutMin;

IF bClamp THEN
    IF rOut > rOutMax THEN rOut := rOutMax;
    ELSIF rOut < rOutMin THEN rOut := rOutMin;
    END_IF
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_TemperatureSensor — Universal Temperature Sensor Interface

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Supports three input types:
   - 4-20mA transmitter (nInputType := 0)
   - 0-10V transmitter  (nInputType := 1)
   - Direct PT100 RTD   (nInputType := 2)

   Features: scaling, wire-break/short detection, high/low alarms
   with hysteresis, first-order filter.

   Usage:
     fbTemp : FB_TemperatureSensor;
     fbTemp(nRawValue := nAD_Ch0, nInputType := 0,
            rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 200.0,
            rAlarmHigh := 180.0, rAlarmLow := 5.0);
     rTemperature := fbTemp.rValue;
     bOverTemp    := fbTemp.bAlarmHigh;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_TemperatureSensor
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    nInputType      : INT := 0;            (* 0=4-20mA, 1=0-10V, 2=PT100 *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Eng. unit at raw min [deg C] *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 200.0;       (* Eng. unit at raw max [deg C] *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* Raw ADC minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* Raw ADC maximum *)
    rAlarmHigh      : REAL := 180.0;       (* High alarm threshold *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 5.0;         (* Low alarm threshold *)
    rWarnHigh       : REAL := 150.0;       (* High warning threshold *)
    rWarnLow        : REAL := 10.0;        (* Low warning threshold *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 2.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.1;         (* Low-pass filter (0.0-1.0) *)
    nWireBreakLow   : INT := 100;          (* Wire break detection: below this = open *)
    nWireBreakHigh  : INT := 32600;        (* Wire break detection: above this = short *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable sensor processing *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Scaled temperature [deg C] *)
    rRawFiltered    : REAL;                (* Filtered raw value *)
    bAlarmHigh      : BOOL;                (* High alarm active *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;               (* Low alarm active *)
    bWarnHigh       : BOOL;                (* High warning active *)
    bWarnLow        : BOOL;                (* Low warning active *)
    bWireBreak      : BOOL;                (* Wire break / open circuit *)
    bShortCircuit   : BOOL;                (* Short circuit detected *)
    bErr          : BOOL;                (* Any error condition *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading is valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rRawReal        : REAL;
    rScaled         : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

rRawReal := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);

(* Wire break / short circuit detection *)
bWireBreak    := nRawValue < nWireBreakLow;
bShortCircuit := nRawValue > nWireBreakHigh;
bErr        := bWireBreak OR bShortCircuit;

IF bErr THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* First-order low-pass filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rRawFiltered := rRawReal;
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rRawFiltered := rRawFiltered + rFilterFactor * (rRawReal - rRawFiltered);
END_IF

(* Linear scaling: raw → engineering units *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rScaled := (rRawFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
               * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
ELSE
    rScaled := rScaleMin;
END_IF
rValue := rScaled;
bValid := TRUE;

(* Alarm evaluation with hysteresis *)
IF rValue >= rAlarmHigh THEN
    bAlarmHigh := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue < (rAlarmHigh - rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmHigh := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN
    bAlarmLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmLow := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue >= rWarnHigh THEN
    bWarnHigh := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue < (rWarnHigh - rHysteresis) THEN
    bWarnHigh := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue <= rWarnLow THEN
    bWarnLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rWarnLow + rHysteresis) THEN
    bWarnLow := FALSE;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
	PT : TIME;
	E : BOOL := TRUE;
	UP : BOOL := TRUE;
	RST : BOOL;
```

```iec-st
	xAct:	REAL;	// measured Value

	LimHigh	: 	REAL; 	// upper limit of output

END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	Y : REAL;		// controller output
	LIM : BOOL;		// True, if output reaches LimLow or LimHigh
END_VAR
VAR
	e			 :  REAL;		// control difference
	yOffset		 :  REAL	:= 0;		// constant offset used on Y
	fbDerivative :  FT_DERIV; 	// function block for derivation
	fbIntegrate  :	FB_Integrate;	// function block for integration

	e_gaintrack	:  REAL;		// control difference for integrator
	Y_gaintrack	:  REAL := 0;	// tracking gain of y for Anti-windup
END_VAR
IF StartY <> yOffset THEN
	yOffset := StartY;
	fbIntegrate(RST:=TRUE, inStart:=inStart);
END_IF
IF RST THEN
	fbIntegrate(RST:=TRUE, inStart:=inStart);
END_IF
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_ScaleInt — Linear INT Value Scaling

   Category:     Utilities
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Maps an input INT from one range to another. Internal

     fbScale : FB_ScaleInt;
     fbScale(nIn := nAdcRaw, nInMin := 0, nInMax := 4095,
             nOutMin := 0, nOutMax := 1000);
     nEngValue := fbScale.nOut;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_ScaleInt
VAR_INPUT
    nIn     : INT;             (* Input value *)
    nInMin  : INT := 0;       (* Input range minimum *)
    nInMax  : INT := 4095;    (* Input range maximum *)
    nOutMin : INT := 0;       (* Output range minimum *)
    nOutMax : INT := 1000;    (* Output range maximum *)
    bClamp  : BOOL := TRUE;   (* Clamp output to OutMin..OutMax *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    nOut    : INT;             (* Scaled output *)
    bErr  : BOOL;            (* Division by zero *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rTemp   : REAL;
    nRange  : INT;
END_VAR

nRange := nInMax - nInMin;
IF nRange = 0 THEN
    bErr := TRUE;
    nOut := nOutMin;
    RETURN;
END_IF

bErr := FALSE;
rTemp := INT_TO_REAL(nIn - nInMin) / INT_TO_REAL(nRange)
         * INT_TO_REAL(nOutMax - nOutMin) + INT_TO_REAL(nOutMin);
nOut := REAL_TO_INT(rTemp);

IF bClamp THEN
    IF nOut > nOutMax THEN nOut := nOutMax;
    ELSIF nOut < nOutMin THEN nOut := nOutMin;
    END_IF
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_SolenoidValve — Solenoid Valve Controller

   Category:     Actuators
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Controls a normally-closed or normally-open solenoid valve
   with optional position feedback sensor and stuck-valve detection.

   Usage:
     fbValve : FB_SolenoidValve;
     fbValve(bOpen := bCmdOpenValve, bFeedback := bDI_ValveOpen,
             tFeedbackDelay := T#2S);
     bValveIsOpen := fbValve.bIsOpen;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_SolenoidValve
VAR_INPUT
    bOpen           : BOOL;                (* Command: open valve *)
    bFeedback       : BOOL;                (* Feedback sensor: valve open *)
    bUseFeedback    : BOOL := FALSE;       (* Enable feedback monitoring *)
    tFeedbackDelay  : TIME := T#2S;        (* Feedback timeout *)
    bNormallyOpen   : BOOL := FALSE;       (* TRUE=NO valve, FALSE=NC valve *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable control *)
    bReset          : BOOL;                (* Reset error *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bSolenoid       : BOOL;                (* Solenoid output *)
    bIsOpen         : BOOL;                (* Valve is open *)
    bIsClosed       : BOOL;                (* Valve is closed *)
    bErr          : BOOL;                (* Stuck valve error *)
    nErrId          : DINT;                 (* 0=OK, 1=Stuck open, 2=Stuck closed *)
END_VAR
VAR
    tonFeedback     : TON;
    bExpectedState  : BOOL;
END_VAR

IF bReset THEN
    bErr := FALSE;
    nErrId := 0;
    tonFeedback(IN := FALSE, PT := tFeedbackDelay);
END_IF

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bSolenoid := bNormallyOpen;  (* De-energize = safe state *)
    bIsOpen := bNormallyOpen;
    bIsClosed := NOT bNormallyOpen;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Drive solenoid *)
IF bNormallyOpen THEN
    bSolenoid := NOT bOpen;  (* Energize to close *)
ELSE
    bSolenoid := bOpen;      (* Energize to open *)
END_IF

(* Status *)
IF bUseFeedback THEN
    bIsOpen := bFeedback;
    bIsClosed := NOT bFeedback;

    (* Stuck detection *)
    bExpectedState := bOpen;
    IF bFeedback <> bExpectedState THEN
        tonFeedback(IN := TRUE, PT := tFeedbackDelay);
        IF tonFeedback.Q AND NOT bErr THEN
            bErr := TRUE;
            IF bOpen AND NOT bFeedback THEN
                nErrId := 2; (* Stuck closed *)
            ELSE
                nErrId := 1; (* Stuck open *)
            END_IF
        END_IF
    ELSE
        tonFeedback(IN := FALSE, PT := tFeedbackDelay);
    END_IF
ELSE
    bIsOpen := bOpen;
    bIsClosed := NOT bOpen;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
VAR CONSTANT

(*
version 1.4	1. dec. 2009
programmer 	hugo

ESR_collect collects esr data from up to 8 esr_mon modules and stroes them in an output array.
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_Totalizer — Flow/Energy Integrator with Reset

   Category:     Utilities
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Integrates a rate value over time (e.g., liters/min → total liters,
   kW → kWh). Uses trapezoidal integration for accuracy.

   Usage:
     fbTotal : FB_Totalizer;
     fbTotal(bEnable := TRUE, rRate := rFlowLitersPerMin,
             tCycleTime := T#100MS, bReset := FALSE);
     rTotalLiters := fbTotal.rTotal;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_Totalizer
VAR_INPUT
    bEnable     : BOOL;                (* Enable integration *)
    rRate       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Rate value [units/time_base] *)
    tCycleTime  : TIME := T#100MS;     (* PLC scan cycle time *)
    rTimeBase   : REAL := 60.0;        (* Rate time base in seconds (60=per minute) *)
    bReset      : BOOL;                (* Reset total to zero *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rTotal      : REAL := 0.0;         (* Accumulated total *)
    rPeakRate   : REAL := 0.0;         (* Peak rate recorded *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rPrevRate   : REAL := 0.0;
    rDtSec      : REAL;
END_VAR

IF bReset THEN
    rTotal := 0.0;
    rPeakRate := 0.0;
    rPrevRate := 0.0;
    RETURN;
END_IF

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    rPrevRate := rRate;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Convert cycle time to seconds *)
rDtSec := TIME_TO_REAL(tCycleTime) / 1000.0;

(* Trapezoidal integration: average of current and previous rate *)
IF rTimeBase > 0.0 THEN
    rTotal := rTotal + ((rRate + rPrevRate) / 2.0) * (rDtSec / rTimeBase);
END_IF

(* Track peak *)
IF rRate > rPeakRate THEN
    rPeakRate := rRate;
END_IF

rPrevRate := rRate;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
	ESR_0, ESR_1, ESR_2, ESR_3, ESR_4, ESR_5, ESR_6, ESR_7 : ARRAY [0..3] OF esr_data;
	rst : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_IN_OUT
	pos : INT;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	ESR_OUT : ARRAY[0..31] OF esr_data;
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
	max_in : INT := 3; 
	max_out : INT := 32; (* number of elements in array *)
END_VAR
VAR
	cnt : INT := -1;
END_VAR

(*
version 1.4	1. dec. 2009
programmer 	hugo
tested by		tobias

ESR_collect collects esr data from up to 8 esr_mon modules and stroes them in an output array.
the output pos will display the position of the last element in the array. if the array is empty, pos = -1
when to buffer is read by followon modules. pos has to be reset to -1
if the array will be full, the buffer will be refilled starting at position 0.
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_LevelSensor — Tank Level Sensor with Alarms

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Monitors liquid level in tanks/reservoirs. Supports continuous
   analog input (4-20mA/0-10V) with high/low alarms and
   optional float switch inputs for redundant level detection.

   Usage:
     fbLevel : FB_LevelSensor;
     fbLevel(nRawValue := nAD_Level,
             rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 100.0,
             rAlarmHigh := 95.0, rAlarmLow := 10.0,
             bFloatHigh := bDI_FloatHigh,
             bFloatLow := bDI_FloatLow);
     rLevelPercent := fbLevel.rValue;
     bRefillNeeded := fbLevel.bAlarmLow;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_LevelSensor
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Level minimum [%] *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 100.0;       (* Level maximum [%] *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* ADC minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* ADC maximum *)
    rAlarmHigh      : REAL := 95.0;        (* High level alarm [%] *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 10.0;        (* Low level alarm [%] *)
    rWarnLow        : REAL := 20.0;        (* Low level warning [%] *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 3.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.05;        (* Filter (slow for level) *)
    bFloatHigh      : BOOL := FALSE;       (* Float switch: high level *)
    bFloatLow       : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Float switch: low level (NC) *)
    bUseFloats      : BOOL := FALSE;       (* Use float switches for alarms *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable sensor *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Level [%] *)
    bAlarmHigh      : BOOL;                (* High level alarm *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;                (* Low level alarm *)
    bWarnLow        : BOOL;                (* Low level warning *)
    bEmpty          : BOOL;                (* Tank empty *)
    bFull           : BOOL;                (* Tank full *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rFiltered       : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rFiltered := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rFiltered := rFiltered + rFilterFactor * (INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue) - rFiltered);
END_IF

(* Scale *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rValue := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
              * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
ELSE
    rValue := rScaleMin;
END_IF

(* Clamp *)
IF rValue > rScaleMax THEN rValue := rScaleMax; END_IF
IF rValue < rScaleMin THEN rValue := rScaleMin; END_IF
bValid := TRUE;

(* Alarms — analog or float switch based *)
IF bUseFloats THEN
    bAlarmHigh := bFloatHigh;
    bAlarmLow  := NOT bFloatLow;  (* NC float: open = low level *)
ELSE
    IF rValue >= rAlarmHigh THEN bAlarmHigh := TRUE;
    ELSIF rValue < (rAlarmHigh - rHysteresis) THEN bAlarmHigh := FALSE; END_IF

    IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN bAlarmLow := TRUE;
    ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN bAlarmLow := FALSE; END_IF
END_IF

(* Warning *)
IF rValue <= rWarnLow THEN bWarnLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rWarnLow + rHysteresis) THEN bWarnLow := FALSE; END_IF

bEmpty := rValue <= rScaleMin + 1.0;
bFull  := rValue >= rScaleMax - 1.0;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_TankHeater — Tank Heater with Thermostat and Freeze Protection

   Category:     Actuators
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   Controls a heating element with thermostat logic (hysteresis),
   overheat protection, freeze protection, dry-run prevention,
   and maximum continuous runtime limit.

   Usage:
     fbHeater : FB_TankHeater;
     fbHeater(
       bEnable   := TRUE,
       bTurnOn   := bCmdHeat,
       rActTemp  := rTankTemperature,
       rSetpoint := 25.0,
       bLevelOK  := bLevelSwitch
     );
     bHeater    := fbHeater.bHeaterElement;
     bTempOK    := fbHeater.bTemperatureOK;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_TankHeater
VAR_INPUT
    bEnable             : BOOL;             (* Enable heater system *)
    bTurnOn             : BOOL;             (* Command to heat *)
    (* Temperature feedback *)
    rActTemp            : REAL;             (* Actual tank temperature [deg C] *)
    rSetpoint           : REAL := 25.0;     (* Target temperature [deg C] *)
    (* Thermostat parameters *)
    rHysteresis         : REAL := 2.0;      (* Hysteresis band [deg C] *)
    rMaxTemp            : REAL := 40.0;     (* Max allowed temperature [deg C] *)
    rMinTemp            : REAL := 5.0;      (* Freeze protection threshold [deg C] *)
    (* Safety *)
    bLevelOK            : BOOL := TRUE;     (* Tank level OK — prevent dry running *)
    tMaxOnTime          : TIME := T#30M;    (* Max continuous heater ON time *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    bHeaterElement      : BOOL;             (* Heater output *)
    bHeating            : BOOL;             (* Heating in progress *)
    bTemperatureOK      : BOOL;             (* Temperature within range *)
    bOverheatAlarm      : BOOL;             (* Over-temperature alarm *)
    bFreezeAlarm        : BOOL;             (* Under-temperature alarm *)
    bTimeoutAlarm       : BOOL;             (* Max ON time exceeded *)
END_VAR
VAR
    bThermostatReq      : BOOL;             (* Internal thermostat state *)
    tonMaxTime          : TON;              (* Max ON timer *)
    tonOverheat         : TON;              (* Overheat confirmation *)
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bHeaterElement := FALSE;
    bHeating := FALSE;
    bTemperatureOK := TRUE;
    bOverheatAlarm := FALSE;
    bFreezeAlarm := FALSE;
    bTimeoutAlarm := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF;

(* ============================================================
   THERMOSTAT LOGIC WITH HYSTERESIS
   ============================================================ *)

(* Turn ON below setpoint - hysteresis *)
IF rActTemp < (rSetpoint - rHysteresis) THEN
    bThermostatReq := TRUE;
END_IF;

(* Turn OFF above setpoint + hysteresis *)
IF rActTemp > (rSetpoint + rHysteresis) THEN
    bThermostatReq := FALSE;
END_IF;

(* ============================================================
   SAFETY CHECKS
   ============================================================ *)

(* Overheat detection — confirmed after 5s *)
tonOverheat(IN := rActTemp > rMaxTemp, PT := T#5S);
bOverheatAlarm := tonOverheat.Q;

(* Freeze protection — always heat if too cold *)
bFreezeAlarm := rActTemp < rMinTemp;

(* Maximum continuous runtime *)
tonMaxTime(IN := bHeaterElement, PT := tMaxOnTime);
bTimeoutAlarm := tonMaxTime.Q;

(* ============================================================
   OUTPUT LOGIC
   ============================================================ *)

(* Heater ON conditions:
   1. Enabled AND commanded on (or freeze protection)
   2. Thermostat requests heat (or freeze protection)
   3. Water level OK (prevent dry-run)
   4. No overheat
   5. Max time not exceeded *)
bHeaterElement := bEnable AND
                  (bTurnOn OR bFreezeAlarm) AND
                  (bThermostatReq OR bFreezeAlarm) AND
                  bLevelOK AND
                  NOT bOverheatAlarm AND
                  NOT bTimeoutAlarm;

bHeating := bHeaterElement;

(* Temperature status *)
bTemperatureOK := (rActTemp >= rMinTemp) AND (rActTemp <= rMaxTemp);

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
FUNCTION_BLOCK RMP_W
VAR_INPUT
	SET : BOOL;
	PT : TIME;
	E : BOOL := TRUE;
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_AnalogInput — Generic Analog Input with Scaling and Filtering

   Category:     Sensors
   Platform:     CODESYS V3.5 (IEC 61131-3)
   Version:      1.0
   Dependencies: None (standard IEC only)

   General-purpose analog input block with linear scaling from
   raw ADC to engineering units, first-order filtering, and
   high/low alarm limits.

   Usage:
     fbPressure : FB_AnalogInput;
     fbPressure(nRawValue := nAD_Ch1,
                rScaleMin := 0.0, rScaleMax := 10.0,
                sUnit := 'bar');
     rPressure := fbPressure.rValue;
   ============================================================= *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_AnalogInput
VAR_INPUT
    nRawValue       : INT;                 (* Raw ADC value *)
    rScaleMin       : REAL := 0.0;         (* Engineering minimum *)
    rScaleMax       : REAL := 100.0;       (* Engineering maximum *)
    nRawMin         : INT := 0;            (* ADC raw minimum *)
    nRawMax         : INT := 32767;        (* ADC raw maximum *)
    rAlarmHigh      : REAL := 90.0;        (* High alarm limit *)
    rAlarmLow       : REAL := 5.0;         (* Low alarm limit *)
    rHysteresis     : REAL := 2.0;         (* Alarm hysteresis *)
    rFilterFactor   : REAL := 0.2;         (* Filter alpha (0.0-1.0) *)
    bEnable         : BOOL := TRUE;        (* Enable processing *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    rValue          : REAL;                (* Scaled value *)
    rPercent        : REAL;                (* 0-100% of scale *)
    bAlarmHigh      : BOOL;                (* High alarm *)
    bAlarmLow       : BOOL;                (* Low alarm *)
    bValid          : BOOL;                (* Reading valid *)
END_VAR
VAR
    rFiltered       : REAL;
    rRange          : REAL;
    bInit           : BOOL := FALSE;
END_VAR

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bValid := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF

(* Filter *)
IF NOT bInit THEN
    rFiltered := INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue);
    bInit := TRUE;
ELSE
    rFiltered := rFiltered + rFilterFactor * (INT_TO_REAL(nRawValue) - rFiltered);
END_IF

(* Scale *)
rRange := INT_TO_REAL(nRawMax - nRawMin);
IF ABS(rRange) > 0.001 THEN
    rValue := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange
              * (rScaleMax - rScaleMin) + rScaleMin;
    rPercent := (rFiltered - INT_TO_REAL(nRawMin)) / rRange * 100.0;
ELSE
    rValue := rScaleMin;
    rPercent := 0.0;
END_IF
bValid := TRUE;

(* Alarms with hysteresis *)
IF rValue >= rAlarmHigh THEN
    bAlarmHigh := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue < (rAlarmHigh - rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmHigh := FALSE;
END_IF

IF rValue <= rAlarmLow THEN
    bAlarmLow := TRUE;
ELSIF rValue > (rAlarmLow + rHysteresis) THEN
    bAlarmLow := FALSE;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

 * This Function Block continuously monitors the superconducting dipole magnet 
 * voltage and temperature. A quench is detected if the resistive voltage across 
 * the coil exceeds the predetermined threshold for a specified duration, or if 
 * the cryogenic helium temperature rises critically. Upon quench detection, 
 * it triggers the Quench Protection System (QPS), fires the quench heaters, 
 * and initiates the energy extraction sequence into the dump resistors.
 *)
FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_QuenchDetectionAndExtraction
VAR_INPUT
    bEnable                 : BOOL;   (* System Enable *)
    rMagnetVoltageA         : REAL;   (* Voltage across magnet half A [V] *)
    rMagnetVoltageB         : REAL;   (* Voltage across magnet half B [V] *)
    rMagnetCurrent          : REAL;   (* Main operating current [A] *)
    rdIdt                   : REAL;   (* Current derivative di/dt [A/s] *)
    rHeliumTemp1            : REAL;   (* Helium temperature sensor 1 [K] *)
    rHeliumTemp2            : REAL;   (* Helium temperature sensor 2 [K] *)
    rInductance             : REAL;   (* Nominal magnet inductance [H] *)
    rVoltageThreshold       : REAL;   (* Resistive voltage threshold for quench [V] *)
    rTempThreshold          : REAL;   (* Critical temperature threshold [K] *)
    tValidationTime         : TIME;   (* Time delay to validate quench condition *)
END_VAR

VAR_OUTPUT
    bQuenchDetected         : BOOL;   (* Quench alarm status *)
    bFireQuenchHeaters      : BOOL;   (* Trigger for quench heaters *)
    bOpenDumpSwitches       : BOOL;   (* Trigger to open extraction switches *)
    bFastPowerAbort         : BOOL;   (* Interlock signal to main power converter *)
    rCalculatedResVoltage   : REAL;   (* Calculated resistive voltage for monitoring [V] *)
    iDumpState              : INT;    (* State of the energy extraction process *)
END_VAR

VAR
    rInductiveVoltage       : REAL;   (* V_ind = L * di/dt *)
    rTotalVoltage           : REAL;   (* V_total = V_A + V_B *)
    rResistiveVoltage       : REAL;   (* V_res = V_total - V_ind *)
    
    TON_QuenchDelay         : TON;    (* Timer to filter noise on voltage signals *)
    TON_TempDelay           : TON;    (* Timer to filter noise on temp signals *)
    
    bVoltageCondition       : BOOL;
    bTempCondition          : BOOL;
    
    rtEnable                : R_TRIG;
END_VAR

(* Logic Implementation *)
rtEnable(CLK := bEnable);

IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bQuenchDetected := FALSE;
    bFireQuenchHeaters := FALSE;
    bOpenDumpSwitches := FALSE;
    bFastPowerAbort := FALSE;
    iDumpState := 0;
    TON_QuenchDelay(IN := FALSE);
    TON_TempDelay(IN := FALSE);
    RETURN;

(* 1. Voltage Monitoring (Resistive Voltage Calculation) *)
(* Calculate total voltage across the magnet *)
rTotalVoltage := rMagnetVoltageA + rMagnetVoltageB;

(* Calculate inductive voltage component (V = L * di/dt) *)
rInductiveVoltage := rInductance * rdIdt;

(* Extract the resistive voltage component (V_res = V_total - V_ind) *)
rResistiveVoltage := ABS(rTotalVoltage - rInductiveVoltage);

```iec-st
(*
version 2.0	23. oct. 2008
programmer 	oscat
tested BY	oscat

this ramp generator generates a Word wide ramp with 65535 steps
the generator has an asynchronous set and reset
the ramp is controlled by PT which is the total ramp time for a full sweep from 0..65535
an UD input controlls the direction Up or Down and the E input enables the ramp generation
a busy output indicates that the ramp is running, busy false means output is stable.
the outputs low and high will be true when the output has reached its max or min value.
*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK RMP_W
VAR_INPUT
	SET : BOOL;
	PT : TIME;
	E : BOOL := TRUE;
	UP : BOOL := TRUE;
	RST : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	out : WORD;
	busy : BOOL;
	high : BOOL;
	low : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
	rmp : _RMP_W;
END_VAR
(* generate ramp *)
rmp(dir := UP, E := E, TR := PT, rmp := out);

(* set or reset operation *)
IF RST THEN
	out := 0;
ELSIF SET THEN
	out := 65535;
END_IF;

(* checks for outputs stable and reset or set busy flag *)
low := out = 0;
high := out = 65535;
busy := NOT (low OR high) AND E;
```

```iec-st
(* =============================================================
   FB_AxisScaler — Axis Unit Conversion (mm/pulses, mm-s/Hz)

   Category:     Motion

     fbScaler(rPitch := 5.0, nPulsesPerRev := 10000, rGearRatio := 1.0);

     rMm     := fbScaler.fnPulsesToPos(nPulses := 200000);

    rPitch          : REAL := 5.0;         (* Lead screw pitch [mm/rev] or [deg/rev] *)
    nPulsesPerRev   : DINT := 10000;       (* Encoder pulses per revolution *)
    rGearRatio      : REAL := 1.0;         (* Gear ratio (motor/load) *)

VAR_OUTPUT

    rPulsesPerMm    : REAL;                (* Conversion factor: pulses per mm *)

    ELSE
        rPulsesPerMm := 0.0;
    END_IF
ELSE
    rMmPerPulse := 0.0;
    rPulsesPerMm := 0.0;
END_IF

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
```

```iec-st
`iec61131-3
(*
======================================================================================
BLOCK: FB_FloatGlassTinBathController
VERSION: 3.2.0
AUTHOR: Lead Manufacturing Engineer - Advanced Glass Foundry Systems
DESCRIPTION:
Comprehensive controller for the Float Glass Tin Bath process. 
Integrates advanced control strategies for:
  1. Ribbon Thickness: Synchronized top-roller speed profiling.
  2. Atmosphere Control: Precise N2/H2 forming gas ratio blending.
  3. Thermal Zoning: Multi-zone thermal gradient management.
======================================================================================
*)

TYPE ST_TopRoller :
STRUCT
    ActualSpeed : REAL; (* m/min *)
    TargetSpeed : REAL; (* m/min *)
    ImmersionDepth : REAL; (* mm *)
    Angle : REAL; (* degrees *)
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

TYPE ST_ThermalZone :
STRUCT
    ActualTemp : REAL; (* deg C *)
    TargetTemp : REAL; (* deg C *)
    HeaterOutput : REAL; (* 0-100% *)
    CoolerOutput : REAL; (* 0-100% *)
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

FUNCTION_BLOCK FB_FloatGlassTinBathController
VAR_INPUT
    (* General Process Variables *)
    bEnable : BOOL;
    fLineSpeed : REAL; (* Primary ribbon line speed (m/min) *)
    
    (* 1. Thickness Control Inputs *)
    fTargetThickness : REAL; (* mm *)
    fActualThickness : REAL; (* mm *)
    aTopRollers_In : ARRAY[1..6] OF ST_TopRoller;
    
    (* 2. Atmosphere Control Inputs *)
    fN2_ActualFlow : REAL; (* Nm3/h *)
    fH2_ActualFlow : REAL; (* Nm3/h *)
    fTargetH2_Ratio : REAL; (* typically 5% to 10% *)
    
    (* 3. Thermal Gradient Zoning Inputs *)
    aZones_In : ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_ThermalZone; 
END_VAR

VAR_OUTPUT
    (* General *)
    bSystemReady : BOOL;
    bAlarm : BOOL;
    
    (* 1. Thickness Control Outputs *)
    aTopRollers_Out : ARRAY[1..6] OF ST_TopRoller;
    
    (* 2. Atmosphere Control Outputs *)
    fN2_ValveCommand : REAL; (* 0-100% *)
    fH2_ValveCommand : REAL; (* 0-100% *)
    
    (* 3. Thermal Gradient Zoning Outputs *)
    aZones_Out : ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_ThermalZone;
END_VAR

VAR
    (* Internal PID Controllers - Using Advanced FB_PID implementations *)
    fbThicknessPID : FB_PID;
    fbH2RatioPID : FB_PID;
    fbZonePID : ARRAY[1..5] OF FB_PID;
    
    (* Internal Variables *)
    i : INT;
    fThicknessCorrection : REAL;
    fTotalGasDemand : REAL := 1500.0; (* Base demand in Nm3/h *)
    fH2_Demand : REAL;
    fN2_Demand : REAL;
    
    (* Constants *)
    MAX_ROLLERS : INT := 6;
    MAX_ZONES : INT := 5;
END_VAR

(* ========================================================= *)
(* INIT & SAFETY CHECKS                                      *)
(* ========================================================= *)
IF NOT bEnable THEN
    bSystemReady := FALSE;
    bAlarm := FALSE;
    RETURN;
END_IF;

bSystemReady := TRUE;

(* ========================================================= *)
(* 1. RIBBON THICKNESS CONTROL (TOP-ROLLER SYNC)             *)
(* ========================================================= *)
(* 
   Thickness is controlled by stretching the glass.
   The top rollers grip the edges of the glass ribbon. 
   Their speed relative to the primary line speed dictates the final thickness.
*)
fbThicknessPID(
    SetPoint := fTargetThickness,
    ActualValue := fActualThickness,
    Kp := 2.5,
    Ki := 0.8,
    Kd := 0.1,
    OutputMin := -10.0, (* Max negative stretch correction *)
    OutputMax := 10.0,  (* Max positive stretch correction *)
    Correction => fThicknessCorrection
);

(* Distribute speed correction across top rollers based on their longitudinal position *)
FOR i := 1 TO MAX_ROLLERS DO
    aTopRollers_Out[i] := aTopRollers_In[i];
    
    (* Roller speed is a function of primary line speed + thickness correction + mechanical profile *)
    (* Downstream rollers (higher index) pull slightly faster to maintain tension *)
    aTopRollers_Out[i].TargetSpeed := fLineSpeed + fThicknessCorrection + (INT_TO_REAL(i) * 0.05);
    
    (* Safety clamp *)
    IF aTopRollers_Out[i].TargetSpeed > (fLineSpeed * 1.5) THEN
        aTopRollers_Out[i].TargetSpeed := (fLineSpeed * 1.5);
    ELSIF aTopRollers_Out[i].TargetSpeed < (fLineSpeed * 0.5) THEN
        aTopRollers_Out[i].TargetSpeed := (fLineSpeed * 0.5);
    END_IF;
END_FOR;

(* ========================================================= *)
(* 2. REDUCING ATMOSPHERE CONTROL (N2/H2 BLENDING)           *)
(* ========================================================= *)
(* 
   Maintain an overpressure reducing atmosphere to prevent tin oxidation.
   Typically a mixture of Nitrogen and Hydrogen. 
*)
fH2_Demand := fTotalGasDemand * (fTargetH2_Ratio / 100.0);
fN2_Demand := fTotalGasDemand - fH2_Demand;

(* H2 Valve Control *)
fbH2RatioPID(
    SetPoint := fH2_Demand,
    ActualValue := fH2_ActualFlow,
    Kp := 1.2,
    Ki := 0.4,
    Kd := 0.0,
    OutputMin := 0.0,
    OutputMax := 100.0,
    Correction => fH2_ValveCommand
);

(* N2 acts as the bulk carrier gas, valve command proportional to demand with trim *)
fN2_ValveCommand := (fN2_Demand / 2000.0) * 100.0; (* Assuming 2000 Nm3/h max capacity *)
IF fN2_ValveCommand > 100.0 THEN fN2_ValveCommand := 100.0; END_IF;

(* Atmosphere Alarms *)
IF (fH2_ActualFlow / (fN2_ActualFlow + 0.1) * 100.0) > 12.0 THEN
    (* Dangerous H2 concentration - Explosion risk *)
    bAlarm := TRUE;
    fH2_ValveCommand := 0.0; (* Shut off H2 immediately *)
END_IF;


(* ========================================================= *)
(* 3. TIN BATH THERMAL GRADIENT ZONING                       *)
(* ========================================================= *)
(*
   The glass must cool from ~1050 C to ~600 C as it floats on the tin.
   Different zones have different heating/cooling requirements.
*)
FOR i := 1 TO MAX_ZONES DO
    aZones_Out[i] := aZones_In[i];
    
    fbZonePID[i](
        SetPoint := aZones_In[i].TargetTemp,
        ActualValue := aZones_In[i].ActualTemp,
        Kp := 5.0,
        Ki := 0.1,
        Kd := 1.5,
        OutputMin := -100.0, (* -100 to 0 is Cooling *)
        OutputMax := 100.0,  (* 0 to 100 is Heating *)
        Correction => aZones_Out[i].HeaterOutput (* Used as a raw output for both here *)
    );
    
    IF fbZonePID[i].Correction > 0.0 THEN
        aZones_Out[i].HeaterOutput := fbZonePID[i].Correction;
        aZones_Out[i].CoolerOutput := 0.0;
    ELSE
        aZones_Out[i].HeaterOutput := 0.0;
        aZones_Out[i].CoolerOutput := ABS(fbZonePID[i].Correction);
    END_IF;
    
    (* Over-temp safety *)
    IF aZones_In[i].ActualTemp > (aZones_In[i].TargetTemp + 50.0) THEN
        bAlarm := TRUE;
    END_IF;
END_FOR;
```

```iec-st
	H : REAL := -0.83333333333;	(* heighth above horizon for sunrise *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
	MIDDAY : TOD;			(*	astrological midday in hours when sun stands at south direction	*)
	SUN_RISE : TOD;				(*	sun rise for current day in local time *)
	SUN_SET : TOD;				(*	sun set for current day in local time *)
	SUN_DECLINATION : REAL;		(*	sun declination above horizon at midday in degrees	*)
END_VAR
VAR
	dk: REAL;						(* sun declination at midday *)
	delta: TIME;					(* delta from midday for sunrise and sunset  *)
	b: REAL;
END_VAR

(*
version 1.7	25. jan. 2011
programmer 	hugo
tested by	tobias

this FUNCTION block calculates the sun rise, sun set, sun offset at midday sun declination for a given date
for performance reasons the algorithm has been simplified and is accurate within a few minutes only
the times are calculated in utc and have to be corrected for the given time zone
this correction is not done within sun_time because it would be a problem on days where dst is enabled or disabled

sun_declination := DEG(DK);

sun_declination := 90.0 - LATITUDE + sun_declination;
delta := HOUR_TO_TIME(ACOS((SIN(RAD(H)) - SIN(B) * SIN(DK)) / (COS(B) * COS(DK))) * 3.819718632);
sun_rise := MIDDAY - delta;
sun_set := MIDDAY + delta;
```
